notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT draft: it is shorter than the prophet drafts, stays inside the event's own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state; the prophet stories (content/stories) are not repeated here. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

chapters.title_en: What God said of his raising

claims.statement_en: God said: O Isa, I am mutawaffika and raising you to Me and purifying you from those who disbelieved, and I will place those who follow you above those who disbelieved until the Day of Resurrection; then to Me is your return and I will judge between you in what you differed.
The ayah reports their claim that they killed the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, the messenger of God.

They did not kill him and did not crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them; those who differ about it are in doubt, have no knowledge of it, and follow only conjecture; they did not kill him for certain.
Rather, God raised him to Himself; God is Mighty, Wise.

chapters.summary_md: God told Isa that He was raising him to Himself and placing those who follow him above those who disbelieved until the Day of Resurrection [c1]. The ayat say that they did not kill him or crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them, and that God raised him to Himself [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md:
God said: O Isa, I am mutawaffika and raising you to Me and purifying you from those who disbelieved [c1]. He said that He would place those who follow him above those who disbelieved until the Day of Resurrection, and that then their return is to Him and He will judge between them in what they differed [c1].

The other passage reports their claim that they killed the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, the messenger of God [c2]. It says that they did not kill him and did not crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them [c3]. Those who differ about it are in doubt, have no knowledge of it, and follow only conjecture; they did not kill him for certain [c3].

Rather, God raised him to Himself; God is Mighty, Wise [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The word mutawaffika is read in more than one way and is left untranslated here [c1]. The ayat give God's raising of him in more than one form: as His address to Isa and as His statement of what is true against the claim [c1][c4]. The ayah on the claim speaks of doubt and conjecture among those who differ about it [c3].
chapters.kids_md: God told Isa that He would raise him to Himself [c1]. Some people claimed they had killed him, but the ayah says they did not, and that God raised him to Himself [c2][c3][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat answer a claim with what is certain, that God raised him to Himself [c3][c4]. Another is that the ayat set doubt and conjecture beside knowledge [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how Isa was raised, where, when, or in what state; the ayat say that God raised him to Himself and no more.
- Not established: what it was that was made to appear so to them; the Arabic is open and the draft keeps it open.
- Not established: the meaning of mutawaffika beyond the Arabic word, which commentators read in more than one way.
- Not established: who the ones who claimed to have killed him are, beyond the ayah's report of their saying.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the raising and on any later return. None is used in this draft.
The word mutawaffika (3:55) and the phrase shubbiha lahum (4:157) are read in more than one way; a scholar must decide how the page words each, and this draft deliberately takes no side.
The order of 3:55 and 4:157-158 is a reading order; the ayat do not give a timeline between them.
